back_translation: The vision of Isaiah son of Amoz, which he saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem, in the reigns of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah.
O heavens, listen! O earth, give ear! For the LORD has spoken: "I have raised children up to be grown and lifted them high, but they have rebelled against Me."
The ox still knows its owner, and the donkey knows the manger of its master, but Israel does not know; My people do not understand."

Oh, nation heavy with sin, a people weighed down with iniquity, a brood of those who do evil, children who behave corruptly! They have forsaken the LORD, have despised the Holy One of Israel, and turned their backs away from Him.
Why will you be beaten again? Why do you still add rebellion further? The head is sick all over; the heart is faint through the whole of it.
From the sole of the foot up to the head there is no part sound at all — only wounds, bruises, and fresh open sores, that have not been pressed clean, not bound up, and not soothed with oil.
Your land is desolate; your cities are burned with fire. As for your fields — foreigners devour them before your very eyes; it is desolate as if overthrown by foreigners.
The Daughter of Zion is left remaining like a shelter in a vineyard, like a watchman's hut in a cucumber field, like a city besieged.
Unless the LORD of Hosts had left survivors for us, a few, we would have become like Sodom; we would have been like Gomorrah already.
O leaders of Sodom, hear the word of the LORD! O people of Gomorrah, give ear to the law/instruction of our God!

"What meaning is the multitude of your sacrifices to Me?" says the LORD. "I am sated with burnt offerings of rams and the fat of fattened beasts; I take no pleasure in the blood of young bulls, lambs, or male goats.
When you come in to appear before Me, who is it that demanded this from your hands — to come trample the courts of My House?

Do not bring worthless grain offerings anymore. Your incense is a detestable thing to Me. New Moons, Sabbaths, and the calling of holy convocations — I cannot bear iniquity paired with the solemn assembly.
My heart hates your New Moons and your appointed festivals. They have become a burden to Me; I am weary of carrying them.
When you spread out your hands in prayer, I will hide My eyes from you. Even though you pray abundantly, I will not listen. Your hands are full of blood.
Wash yourselves; make yourselves clean. Take your evil deeds away out of My sight. Cease doing evil.
Learn to do good; seek justice; restrain the oppressor; give fair judgment to the fatherless child; plead the case on behalf of the widow."
"Come, let us consider the case together," says the LORD. "Though your sins are like bright red, they will be white as snow; though they are deep red like dye from the worm, they will be like wool.
If you are willing and obedient, you will eat the good produce of the land.
But if you refuse and resist, you will be devoured by the sword." For the mouth of the LORD has spoken.
Oh, how the city that was once faithful has become a prostitute! She was once full of justice; righteousness once lodged in her — but now there are only murderers.
Your silver has become dross; your fine wine is adulterated with water.

Your princes are rebellious-stubborn ones and companions of thieves. Everyone loves a bribe and chases after gifts-of-payment. They do not give fair judgment to the fatherless child, and the legal case of the widow never reaches them.
Therefore the Sovereign Master, the LORD of Hosts, the Mighty One of Israel, declares: "Ah, I will vent My indignation on My adversaries and avenge Myself on My enemies.
I will turn My hand against you; I will smelt away your dross until it is purged as if cleansed with lye, and will remove all your alloy-impurities.
I will restore your judges to be as at the first, and your counselors as at the beginning. After that you will be given the name 'City of Righteousness, Faithful City.'"
Zion will be redeemed with justice, and those of her who turn back, with righteousness.
But the rebels and the sinners will be shattered together, and those who forsake the LORD will utterly perish.
For they will be ashamed because of the oaks that you so desired, and you will be disgraced because of the gardens that you have chosen.
For you will be like an oak whose leaves wither, and like a garden that has no water.
The strong one will become flax-fiber tow, and his work a spark; the two of them will burn up together, with no one able to quench it.
